chunks: Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام was asked about salat (prayer) in synagogues and churches, so he said: “Pray in them.”
He said: So I said: Even if they are praying in them, should I pray in them? He said: “Yes. Do you not recite the Qur’an:
“Say: Each acts according to his manner, but your Lord knows best who is best guided in way.”
Pray facing the qiblah and leave them.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the act being asked about
key_terms.الْبِيَعِ: synagogues or non-Muslim houses of worship
key_terms.الْقُرْآنَ: the Qur’an cited as proof in the ruling
key_terms.شَاكِلَتِهِ: one’s manner, way, or disposition of acting
key_terms.وَدَعْهُمْ: leave them; do not concern yourself with their practice

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in churches and synagogues in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling permitting salat (prayer) in synagogues and churches. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructs the believer to face the qiblah and not be concerned with the worship practices of others, and he cites a Qur’anic verse emphasizing that each people act according to their own way while Allah knows best who is rightly guided.
